findings.title: aws_amplify_app never sets custom_headers, leaving hosted sites without baseline security response headers
findings.explanation: aws_amplify_app supports a custom_headers attribute for injecting CSP, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options and Strict-Transport-Security into every response, but this module neither sets it nor exposes it as a variable. Deterministic engines have no rule for this resource type at all (it is absent from coverage_by_type), so the gap is invisible to holden's rule set. Every site deployed through this reusable module inherits Amplify Hosting's default of no security response headers, exposing consumers to clickjacking and content-sniffing risks unless they fork the module to add them.
findings.remediation: Add a `custom_headers` variable (default to a sane baseline: X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, Strict-Transport-Security, and a CSP) and wire it into the `aws_amplify_app.pike` resource so consumers get secure headers by default and can override per app.

findings.title: environment_variables is a plain, non-sensitive map(string) with no guidance away from storing secrets in it
findings.explanation: The `app` variable's `environment_variables` field (variables.tf:7, wired to aws_amplify_app.tf:16) is typed map(string) with no `sensitive = true` and no documented alternative. AWS Amplify Hosting has no built-in secret manager for these values — anything placed here is stored in plaintext in Terraform state, in `terraform plan` output/CI logs, and is readable in the Amplify console by anyone with app read access. Because the module's own default already sets an env var (`ENV = "test"`), it establishes environment_variables as the expected place to pass build-time config, which invites consumers to also drop real secrets (API keys, tokens) there rather than referencing SSM Parameter Store from the buildspec.
findings.remediation: Mark the `environment_variables` field (or the whole `app` variable) `sensitive = true`, and document/recommend referencing AWS SSM Parameter Store or Secrets Manager from `build_spec` commands instead of passing secrets through environment_variables directly.

suggested_policies.rationale: aws_amplify_app has zero deterministic coverage in holden today (absent from coverage_by_type entirely). custom_headers is a well-defined, unambiguous attribute path: either the app defines response security headers or it relies entirely on Amplify Hosting's insecure default of none. This is a concrete, broadly applicable attribute check, not an intent/context judgment, so it fits the existing not_null DSL cleanly.
suggested_policies.yaml:
id: HLD_PROPOSED_001
name: Amplify app should configure custom security response headers
principle: governance
severity: MEDIUM
rationale: |
  AWS Amplify Hosting does not inject any security response headers by default. Without a custom_headers configuration, deployed sites are served without Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, or Strict-Transport-Security, leaving them exposed to clickjacking, MIME-sniffing, and reduced XSS mitigation. This is easy to overlook because the app deploys and functions normally without it.
remediation: |
  Add a custom_headers block to the aws_amplify_app resource defining at minimum X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Strict-Transport-Security, and a Content-Security-Policy appropriate to the app.
resources:
  aws_amplify_app:
    path: custom_headers
    not_null: true
